current_rule.summary: Each configured provider endpoint must appear exactly in a hash-bound capture fetched from an HTTPS official provider-family host; redirect, cache, DNS, TLS, runtime behavior, or third-party publication alone is insufficient.

triggering_transport_evidence.interpretation: Transport capability and semantic agreement are established for the frozen fixtures, but provider identity and independence are not established by this report.

official_sources.qualifier: This supports the Ethereum endpoint-to-operator link, subject to accountable identity and independence review.
The published endpoint did not resolve during the same check and is not the transport-tested https://bsc.merkle.io endpoint.
This is not the transport-tested https://base.merkle.io endpoint and cannot be exercised without a Blink API key.
Search indexes retain an older page naming eth.merkle.io and bsc.merkle.io, but the live source redirects; cached search content is not accepted as a current capture.

current_source_check.conclusion: The frozen exact-publication rule can presently bind eth.merkle.io from a current first-party page, but it cannot bind the transport-tested base.merkle.io or bsc.merkle.io endpoints from a current exact first-party publication.

requirements: Supply CHRONOS_ALCHEMY_API_KEY and CHRONOS_INFURA_API_KEY, a Blink API key for the documented endpoints, or another two-family set with current exact official endpoint publication.
Rebuild and independently verify the provider identity revision.
Rerun the frozen known-creation trace and cutoff-state capability probe before any activation.
options.consequence: No provider-identity exception is introduced; canonical RPC activation remains blocked until documented runtime endpoints are available.

required_conjunctive_evidence: A current first-party merkle.io page binds the Merkle domain to Blink Labs branding and current official Blink documentation or portal links.
A current first-party Blink source establishes support for the relevant chain, even when it publishes a replacement endpoint rather than the legacy endpoint.
The exact legacy endpoint remains under the merkle.io registrable domain and passes live DNS, TLS-hostname, HTTPS, and expected eth_chainId checks at freeze time.
The exact legacy endpoint passes the frozen historical block, receipt, trace, EIP-1898 runtime-code, and three proxy-slot fixture checks with hash-bound raw request and response envelopes.
The paired non-Merkle family has separately exact-published endpoint evidence and no identified common operator ownership with Blink Labs.

An accountable reviewer signs the exact endpoint, operator-family, chain, evidence hashes, limitations, and expiry after reviewing identity and independence; local key possession alone is not identity proof.
fail_closed_rules: Any failed or unavailable conjunct is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
The rule does not generalize to another hostname, chain, provider family, date, or production track.
The rule does not establish archive capability beyond the exact frozen probes.
The rule cannot authorize selection, qualification, counters, stage promotion, Recovery3 mutation, release eligibility, or independent review.
Canonical scientific activation remains false unless the existing accountable provider-identity and separate RPC-activation gates also pass.
options.consequence: If explicitly approved and implemented, the legacy endpoints may be used only to continue a labeled local-test trace/cutoff-state run; canonical counters remain fail-closed.
